title: Spire and Veil
premise: Noor Ravensworth, exiled for a storm-calling that killed the wrong people, keeps ledgers for the Gilded Veil, a guild trading in impossible things: bottled memories, borrowed years, names that were never spoken. When a dying courier presses a map of the Sunken Spire into Noor's hands, they discover it charts not treasure but the prison of the Veil's founder — and the secret of how the long winter began. Hunted by the guild's enforcers and shadowed by a memory-thief who wears stolen faces, Noor must choose between reclaiming their erased past and destroying the map before the guild's mistress uses it to reignite the war that froze the world. In the end, Noor gives up their own memories to seal the Spire forever, surviving the winter as a stranger even to themselves — alive, but at the price the title promises.
about_author: Paloma Thornbury is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing damaged manuscripts in northern university libraries, where the winters shaped her imagination as much as her reading did. She writes fantasy about people who survive things they should not have survived, and what survival costs them.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: Noor Ravensworth catalogs a shipment of bottled memories for the Gilded Veil guild, revealing their exile from the storm-calling city of Aerhallow and their careful, colorless life among the guild's clerks. POV: Noor. Emotional beat: quiet loneliness disguised as competence.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Salt Door
chapters.summary: A frost-bitten courier collapses into the guildhouse's back alley and presses a wax-sealed map into Noor's hands, whispering 'the Spire remembers' before dying. Guild enforcers arrive minutes too late, and Noor lies about the map for the first time in their careful life. POV: Noor. Emotional beat: fear and the thrill of a first transgression.

chapters.title: What the Map Refuses to Show
chapters.summary: Noor studies the map by candlelight, finding it drawn on vellum made of something that bleeds when cut, its routes shifting when unobserved. A memory bottle they cataloged earlier hums in sympathy with it. POV: Noor. Emotional beat: dread mixed with irresistible curiosity.

chapters.title: Mistress Corvane's Courtesy
chapters.summary: Guildmistress Sable Corvane summons Noor, probing gently about the dead courier while offering promotion — a gilded cage. Noor realizes she suspects more than she says, and that refusing her is as dangerous as obeying. POV: Noor. Emotional beat: suffocating politeness over mutual threat.

chapters.title: The Thief with Borrowed Faces
chapters.summary: A stranger named Wren Ashgrave corners Noor, wearing the face of a clerk Noor buried last spring; Wren is a memory-thief hunting the same map, claiming the courier was their brother. Uneasy alliance forms out of mutual blackmail. POV: Noor. Emotional beat: distrust sharpening into reluctant partnership.

chapters.title: Ledger Entries in Someone Else's Hand
chapters.summary: Noor discovers entries in the guild's oldest ledger written in their own handwriting — records of a night in Aerhallow they cannot remember, dated after their exile supposedly ended. The map may be tied to their own erased past. POV: Noor. Emotional beat: vertigo of self-doubt.

chapters.title: Departure Before the Passes Close
chapters.summary: With the first true snows falling and Corvane dispatching enforcers northward, Noor and Wren flee the guildhouse along the map's first route, through the salt marshes where drowned villages remember their own names aloud. POV: alternating Noor and Wren. Emotional beat: exhilaration curdling into commitment.

chapters.title: The Village That Sold Its Summer
chapters.summary: In a village that traded its warm seasons to the Veil decades ago, Noor witnesses the human cost of impossible trade: children who have never seen green. They buy passage with a bottled memory and hate themselves for the commerce. POV: Noor. Emotional beat: guilt and moral awakening.

chapters.title: Wren's Stolen Childhood
chapters.summary: Wren confesses they stole faces because their own memories were sold to the Veil as collateral; they don't know if their grief for their brother is real or purchased. Noor recognizes a fellow survivor of the guild's arithmetic. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: raw vulnerability forging trust.

chapters.title: Enforcers on the Frozen Road
chapters.summary: Corvane's enforcers ambush them at a mountain waystation; Noor, terrified of their own storm-calling, nearly lets Wren die rather than use it. When they finally call lightning, they enjoy it — and that frightens them more than the enforcers did. POV: Noor. Emotional beat: terror of one's own power and appetite.

chapters.title: The Cartographer's Grave
chapters.summary: Following the map to its maker's tomb, they learn the map was drawn by the Veil's founder, Ilyen Vosk, who imprisoned herself in the Sunken Spire to stop the war she started — and started the winter to freeze the war in place. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: awe and horror reframing the quest.

chapters.title: Corvane Catches Up
chapters.summary: Corvane arrives not with soldiers but alone, revealing she was Vosk's apprentice and has spent two centuries arranging this journey; she needs someone with storm-blood to open the Spire's gates. She offers Noor their erased memories back. POV: Noor. Emotional beat: temptation dressed as restoration.

chapters.title: The Bargain at the Icefall
chapters.summary: Cornered between Corvane and an avalanche, Noor bargains: they will open the Spire, but Corvane must free every memory the Veil holds hostage. All three parties descend toward the coast under an armed truce. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: brittle hope inside a trap.

chapters.title: Harbor of the Drowned Bells
chapters.summary: At the frozen harbor nearest the Spire, the locals worship the winter as divine punishment and try to sacrifice Noor as a storm-witch; Wren burns their own most precious stolen memory to buy the crowd's mercy. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: sacrifice deepening the bond.

chapters.title: Beneath the Ice, the Spire Sings
chapters.summary: Crossing the sea ice, Noor hears the Spire singing in their dead mother's voice — the prison reaching for the one bloodline that can unmake it. They understand now why their memories were taken: they are Vosk's descendant. POV: Noor. Emotional beat: identity collapsing into inheritance.

chapters.title: The Gate That Costs a Name
chapters.summary: The Spire's gate demands a true name freely given; Noor speaks theirs and feels part of themselves go silent forever. Inside, corridors are lined with frozen moments of the ancient war, still fighting in miniature. POV: Noor. Emotional beat: irrevocable loss as the price of entry.

chapters.title: Ilyen Vosk, Still Dreaming
chapters.summary: They find Vosk suspended in the Spire's heart, dreaming the winter to keep the war asleep; she offers Noor a choice framed as mercy: let her die and end the winter, and the war wakes with her. Corvane moves to kill her anyway. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: the revelation that there is no clean answer.

chapters.title: Betrayal in the Heart of Winter
chapters.summary: Corvane reveals her true aim: not ending the winter but inheriting Vosk's power to finish the old war on her terms. She seizes the dream, and the frozen battle-scenes in the walls begin to thaw and scream. POV: Noor. Emotional beat: betrayal and the collapse of every plan.

chapters.title: Storm Over the Sunken Spire
chapters.summary: Noor calls the storm they swore off, tearing the Spire open to the sky; Wren fights Corvane through the thawing war-corridors while Noor climbs toward Vosk's dreaming heart. The climax is paid for in blood and memory alike. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: desperate, costly courage.

chapters.title: The Choice of the Ledger-Keeper
chapters.summary: At the heart, Noor understands the only seal strong enough: a willing memory-sacrifice from Vosk's own blood. They pour their entire past — exile, guilt, mother's voice — into the dream, taking Vosk's place as the winter's keeper. POV: Noor. Emotional beat: tragic transcendence, the theme made flesh.

chapters.title: Thaw
chapters.summary: The war stays sealed, the long winter finally breaks, and Corvane — stripped of her prize — retreats to rebuild the Veil around the empty Spire. Wren carries an amnesiac Noor south, keeping watch over someone who no longer knows them. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: grief braided with tenderness.

chapters.title: New Ledgers, Blank Pages
chapters.summary: Months later, Noor works again as a clerk in a thawing port town, haunted by feelings without sources, while Wren visits with stories they mostly refuse to confirm. In a drawer, Noor finds a map fragment and feels something stir. Some prices, the book suggests, are not finished being paid. POV: Noor. Emotional beat: bittersweet hope with an open door.
